title: Prior Convicted Orleans Parish Sex Offender Sentenced for Possession of Child Sex Abuse Materials
body: Press Release Prior Convicted Orleans Parish Sex Offender Sentenced for Possession of Child Sex Abuse Materials Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Eastern District of Louisiana shane.jones@usdoj.gov NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA – DAVID MOREL (“MOREL”) , age 43, of New Orleans, was sentenced on October 14, 2026, for Possession of Materials Involving the Sexual Exploitation of Minors, in violation of Title 18, United States Code, Sections 2252(a)(4)(B) and (a)(2), announced U.S. Attorney David I. Courcelle. According to court documents, beginning at an unknown time, and continuing until October 20, 2025, MOREL was found in possession of images of pre-pubescent child pornography. MOREL’s home was searched by state law enforcement officials and federal agents on October 20, 2025. MOREL was arrested during the execution of the search warrant by Louisiana Bureau of Investigation agents, after they found him in possession of electronic devices containing media depicting the sexual abuse of prepubescent children. Through a partnership between state and federal authorities, the U.S. Attorney’s Office adopted the state charges. MOREL was previously convicted in federal court by the U.S. Attorney’s Office in 2016 for Possessing Materials Involving the Sexual Exploitation of Minors and was sentenced to one-hundred twenty (120) months in prison. MOREL was sentenced by United States District Judge Jay C. Zainey to ten (10) years imprisonment followed by a life term of supervised release. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice. Led by United States Attorney’s Offices and the Criminal Division’s Child Exploitation and Obscenity Section (CEOS), Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims. For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit www.projectsafechildhood.gov. U.S. Attorney Courcelle praised the work of the U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Homeland Security Investigations, and the Louisiana Bureau of Investigation. The prosecution of this case is being handled by Brian M. Klebba, Deputy Chief of the Criminal Division, Project Safe Childhood Coordinator, and Chief of the Financial Crimes Unit. title: Oahu Man Sentenced to 22 Years in Prison for Producing Child Pornography
body: Press Release Oahu Man Sentenced to 22 Years in Prison for Producing Child Pornography Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Hawaii HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that David Yamamoto, 28, of Waipahu, Hawaii, was sentenced yesterday by United States District Judge Shanlyn A.S. Park to 264 months in federal prison for the production of child pornography, followed by 10 years of supervised release.  District Judge Park remanded Yamamoto into custody immediately at the end of sentencing. According to court records, from in or around 2023 to 2025, Yamamoto used online gaming and messaging applications to find and groom children located in the United States and in foreign countries to send him sexually explicit videos and images of themselves.  Yamamoto misrepresented his age by posing as a teenager on gaming applications geared towards teens and preteens.  He then offered and sent money and gifts to over ten children as payment for engaging in sexually explicit live stream video calls with him and for sending sexually explicit imagery of themselves at his direction. Yamamoto exchanged tens of thousands of online messages with minors, ranging in age from ten to seventeen years old.  In messaging minors, he directed them to expose their genitals in particular poses or insert objects into their genitals, create sexually explicit videos involving urination and masturbation, and recreate images of explicit adult pornography that he had sent to the minors. “The devastating harm Yamamoto inflicted on his numerous victims can never be undone, but his 22-year sentence sends a potent message that those who prey upon our children will face harsh penalties in federal court,” said U.S. Attorney Ken Sorenson.  “Along with our steadfast partners at FBI, we will continue to hunt down child predators like Yamamoto and bring them to justice.” “This sentence sends a clear message to any individuals who exploit children online: the FBI will find you, and you will face justice,” said FBI Honolulu Acting Special Agent in Charge Ryan C. Noonan.  “Yamamoto preyed on minors by hiding behind technology, but his actions did not go unseen.  The FBI and our federal partners remain steadfast in our mission to safeguard children and to pursue those who would harm them, wherever they are and however they operate.” The FBI investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Rebecca A. Perlmutter prosecuted the case. This case was brought as part of Project Safe Childhood, a nationwide initiative to combat the growing epidemic of child sexual exploitation and abuse launched in May 2006 by the Department of Justice.  Led by U.S. Attorneys’ Offices and CEOS, Project Safe Childhood marshals federal, state, and local resources to better locate, apprehend and prosecute individuals who exploit children via the Internet, as well as to identify and rescue victims.  For more information about Project Safe Childhood, please visit Justice.gov/PSC . Contact Aislinn Affinito Aislinn.Affinito@usdoj.gov Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Project Safe Childhood Component USAO - Hawaii

title: Bronx man going to prison for bank fraud conspiracy and ID theft
body: Press Release Bronx man going to prison for bank fraud conspiracy and ID theft Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of New York BUFFALO, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Michael Herrera, 45, of the Bronx, NY, who was convicted of conspiracy to commit bank fraud and aggravated identity theft, was sentenced to serve 54 months in prison by U.S. District Judge Richard J. Arcara. In January 2025, in Bridgeport, Connecticut, co-conspirator Vance Ashley was recruited by members of the conspiracy to pose as other persons and make unauthorized withdrawals from the other persons’ bank accounts. Ashley agreed to do this in exchange for money. Between January 28 and February 3, 2025, Ashley drove with Herrera, and two other co-conspirators, to bank branches in Wilmington, Delaware, Liberty, NY, and Lock Haven, PA, where Ashely used the identifications of other individuals to make, or attempt to make, unauthorized withdrawals from the victims’ bank accounts. On February 5, 2025, the defendants drove to a Northwest Bank branch in Lockport, within the Western District of New York. Ashley made an unauthorized withdrawal of from the account of an individual residing in Erie, PA. Ashley also purchased a bank check using funds from the account. That same day, the defendants drove to another Northwest Bank branch in Williamsville, within the Western District of New York, and again Ashley made an unauthorized withdrawal from an account and purchased a bank check using funds from the account of a victim from North East PA. Also on February 5, 2025, Hererra illegally used the identification of another person during the commission of a felony. The total loss amount, including actual loss and intended loss, is $91,300.00. Ashley was previously convicted and sentenced to serve 27 months in prison. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Paul E. Bonanno. The sentencing is the result of an investigation by the Internal Revenue Service, Criminal Investigation Division, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Harry Chavis and Homeland Security Investigations, under the direction of Acting Special Agent-in-Charge Anthony Patrone. # # # # Contact Barbara Burns 716-843-5817 Updated October 16, 2026 Topics Financial Fraud Identity Theft Component USAO - New York, Western

title: Father and Daughter Admit Roles in Conspiracy to Violate Clean Air Act
body: Press Release Father and Daughter Admit Roles in Conspiracy to Violate Clean Air Act Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – Ricky Jesus Rodriguez and his daughter, Jasmine Rodriguez, pleaded guilty in federal court today, admitting they participated in a months-long conspiracy to smuggle banned refrigerants from Mexico into the United States on behalf of American air conditioning companies. Ricky Rodriguez admitted that he was paid tens of thousands of dollars to coordinate the smuggling of R-22, a hydrochlorofluorocarbon long banned from production and import in the United States.  He admitted that he recruited others, including his daughter, to join the smuggling ring, and helped coordinate her role as well. R-22 is strictly regulated by an international treaty known as the Montreal Protocol that has been ratified by nearly every country. Hydrochlorofluorocarbons like R-22 have an extremely deleterious effect on the ozone layer.  Stratospheric ozone forms a protective shield around the earth that absorbs the sun’s harmful ultraviolet radiation that otherwise causes skin cancer, eye damage, and environmental damage.  R-22, when released into the atmosphere, destroys ozone, depletes the protective ozone layer, and reduces the atmosphere’s ability to block harmful UV radiation.  R-22 had been used as a refrigerant until its use was phased out after these harmful effects were recognized. Despite the ban, at least two HVAC companies recruited and paid Rodriguez, his daughter and other smugglers to hide tanks of R-22 in their cars and drive them across the border. Ricky Rodriguez began smuggling R-22 in the summer of 2023. He admitted he smuggled the chemicals dozens of times, bringing five to ten tanks each time, earning thousands of dollars in smuggling fees. Ricky Rodriguez recruited more smugglers to work for him and the HVAC companies.  His daughter was a driver for the HVAC companies, collecting a smuggling fee for each tank of R-22 she brought into the United States from Mexico. Ricky Rodriguez is scheduled to be sentenced on January 11, 2027, at 10 a.m. before U.S. District Judge Benjamin J. Cheeks.  Jasmine Rodriguez entered into a plea agreement that allows her to defer entry of judgment if she meets conditions of release and remains on good behavior for a period of 12 months, after which her case would be dismissed. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California and the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency are members of the Department of Justice’s Trade Fraud Task Force, a cross-agency law enforcement effort that also involves the National Fraud Enforcement Division, the Criminal and Civil Divisions, the Energy and Natural Resources Division, the Department of Homeland Security, and U.S. Attorney’s Offices nationwide. The Task Force was created to leverage all of the Department’s tools and authorities to prevent trade fraud that deprives the government of vital revenue, threatens critical domestic industries, undermines consumer confidence, and weakens national security.  The Task Force is designed to pursue enforcement actions against parties who seek to evade tariffs and other duties, as well as smugglers who seek to import prohibited goods into the American economy. The Justice Department encourages whistleblowers to alert the government to credible allegations of fraud, including utilizing the qui tam provisions of the False Claims Act or through the Criminal Division’s Corporate Whistleblower Program at CorporateWhistleblower@usdoj.gov using the form available here . This case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorneys Eric Chiang and Emily W. Allen from the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California. The Environmental Protection Agency – Criminal Investigations Division is investigating this case with assistance from Homeland Security Investigations. DEFENDANTS Ricky Jesus Rodriguez, Case No. 26-cr-4089-BJC                Age: 47           San Diego, CA Jasmine Rodriguez, Case No. 26-cr-4089-BJC                      Age: 24           San Diego, CA SUMMARY OF CHARGES Conspiracy to Violate the Clean Air Act – Title 18, U.S.C., Section 371 Maximum penalty: Five years in prison and $250,000 fine INVESTIGATING AGENCY U.S. Environmental Protection Agency Homeland Security Investigations Contact Kelly Thornton, Director of Media Relations Updated October 16, 2026 Topic Environment Component USAO - California, Southern Press Release Number: CAS26-1016-Rodriguez

title: Depew man sentenced for entering secure area at the Buffalo Niagara International Airport
body: Press Release Depew man sentenced for entering secure area at the Buffalo Niagara International Airport Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of New York BUFFALO, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that James R. Muench Jr., 47, of Depew, NY, who was convicted of entering aircraft or aircraft area, was sentenced to serve five years’ probation and ordered to pay a $5,000 fine by U.S. Magistrate Judge H. Kenneth Schroeder, Jr. On May 20, 2025, Muench drove his vehicle up to a closed security gate outside the Buffalo Niagara International Airport. He initially stopped at the gate, but then repeatedly rammed his vehicle into the gate, eventually bending the metal gate. Muench then drove his vehicle through the damaged and partially open gate and continued onto the aircraft operational area of the airport. Muench drove through various secure parts of the airport including the inner airfield roads, aircraft taxiways, the commercial passenger aircraft ramp area, and the active airport runways, where aircraft take off and land. The case was prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Franz M. Wright. The sentencing is the result of an investigation by the Niagara Frontier Transportation Authority Police, under the direction of Chief Brian Patterson and the FBI, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. Davis, II. # # # # Contact Barbara Burns 716-843-5817 Updated October 16, 2026 Component USAO - New York, Western

title: Java Center man pleads guilty to possession of child pornography
body: Press Release Java Center man pleads guilty to possession of child pornography Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Western District of New York BUFFALO, N.Y.-U.S. Attorney Michael DiGiacomo announced today that Patrick Kerwin, 43, of Java Center, NY, pleaded guilty before U.S. District Judge John L. Sinatra, Jr. to possession of child pornography involving a prepubescent minor. The charge carries a maximum penalty of 20 years in prison and a $250,000 fine. According to the plea agreement, on November 19, 2025, Lancaster Police officers encountered Kerwin at a local restaurant where he advised them that he had exchanged text messages with underage girls, possessed child pornography on his cell phone, and that he had been involved in previous “underage relationships.” Kerwin subsequently consented to the seizure and search of his cell phone and voluntarily agreed to be interviewed at the Lancaster Police Department, during which he admitted that he messaged underage girls using social media and encrypted applications. A forensic review of his cell phone recovered 13 images and 81 videos of child pornography. Some of the images and videos depicted the sexual abuse of an infant or toddler, as well as depictions of violence. The case is being prosecuted by Assistant U.S. Attorney Maeve E. Huggins. The plea is the result of an investigation by the FBI, under the direction of Special Agent-in-Charge Allen D. title: Waimanalo Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison for Distributing Methamphetamine
body: Press Release Waimanalo Man Sentenced to Ten Years in Prison for Distributing Methamphetamine Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Hawaii HONOLULU – United States Attorney Ken Sorenson announced that John Junior Fritz, 48, of Waimanalo, Hawaii, was sentenced yesterday by Senior United States District Judge J. Michael Seabright to 120 months in federal prison for possession with the intent to distribute methamphetamine, followed by 5 years of supervised release. According to court documents, in April 2025, Fritz was arrested by the Honolulu Police Department driving a stolen car that contained approximately two pounds of methamphetamine and other drug distribution paraphernalia.  As part of his ongoing drug trafficking, Fritz obtained two to three pounds of methamphetamine every few days for distribution into the community and for his personal use. While on pretrial release, Fritz absconded from Sand Island Treatment Center.  He was arrested three months later and detained pending sentencing. The Drug Enforcement Administration and the Honolulu Police Department investigated the case. Assistant U.S. Attorney Rebecca A. Perlmutter prosecuted the case. This case is part of Operation Take Back America a nationwide initiative that marshals the full resources of the Department of Justice to repel the invasion of illegal immigration, achieve the total elimination of cartels and transnational criminal organizations (TCOs), and protect our communities from the perpetrators of violent crime. title: U.S. Attorney’s Office Filed 111 Border-Related Cases This Week
body: Press Release U.S. Attorney’s Office Filed 111 Border-Related Cases This Week Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               Southern District of California Kelly.Thornton@usdoj.gov SAN DIEGO – Federal prosecutors in the Southern District of California filed 111 border-related cases this week, including charges of bringing in aliens for financial gain, reentering the U.S. after deportation, and importation of controlled substances. The U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Southern District of California is the fourth-busiest federal district, largely due to a high volume of border-related crimes. This district, encompassing San Diego and Imperial counties, shares a 140-mile border with Mexico. It includes the San Ysidro Port of Entry, the world’s busiest land border crossing, connecting San Diego (America’s eighth largest city) and Tijuana (Mexico’s second largest city). In addition to reactive border-related crimes, the Southern District of California also prosecutes a significant number of proactive cases related to terrorism, organized crime, drugs, white-collar fraud, violent crime, cybercrime, human trafficking and national security. Recent developments in those and other significant areas of prosecution can be found here . A sample of border-related arrests this week: On October 11, Rafael Perez Rosario, a Mexican national, was arrested and charged with Deported Alien Found in the United States. According to a complaint, U.S. Border Patrol agents discovered Perez Rosario hiding in a bush in a remote area near the U.S.-Mexico border, approximately two miles east of the Otay Mesa Port of Entry. He was apprehended after a foot chase. Perez Rosario was previously being deported to Mexico on August 5, 2026. On October 12, Lemuel Muniz-Valle, a United States citizen, was arrested and charged with Importation of a Controlled Substance. According to a complaint, Customs and Border Protection officers discovered approximately 115 pounds of methamphetamine concealed inside the doors, dashboard and fuel tank of the 2016 Honda Accord he was driving as he applied for entry to the U.S. at the San Ysidro Port of Entry. On October 14, Summer Smith, a United States citizen, was arrested and charged with Importation of a Controlled Substance. According to a complaint, Smith had 139 grams of fentanyl hidden under clothing as she attempted to cross the border at the San Ysidro Port of Entry pedestrian lanes. The immigration cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including Homeland Security Investigations (HSI), Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE ERO), Customs and Border Protection, U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI), the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF), with the support and assistance of state and local law enforcement partners. Indictments and criminal complaints are merely allegations and all defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: District of Arizona Charges 279 Individuals for Immigration-Related Criminal Conduct this Week
body: Press Release District of Arizona Charges 279 Individuals for Immigration-Related Criminal Conduct this Week Friday, October 16, 2026 Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email For Immediate Release U.S. Attorney's Office,               District of Arizona PHOENIX, Ariz. – During the week of enforcement operations from Oct. 10 through Oct. 16, 2026, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the District of Arizona brought immigration-related criminal charges against 279 individuals. Specifically, the United States filed 136 cases in which aliens illegally re-entered the United States, and the United States also charged 123 aliens for illegally entering the United States. In its ongoing effort to deter unlawful immigration, the United States filed 17 cases against 20 individuals responsible for smuggling illegal aliens into and within the District of Arizona. These cases were referred or supported by federal law enforcement partners, including U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s Enforcement and Removal Operations (ICE-ERO), ICE- Homeland Security Investigations (ICE-HSI), U.S. Border Patrol, the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), the FBI, the U.S. Marshals Service (USMS), and the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF). Recent matters of interest include: United States v. Calixtro-Rodriguez et al. Jesus Manuel Calixtro-Rodriguez and Julio Cesar Ramos-Mendez were charged by criminal complaint on Oct. 13, 2026, with Conspiracy to Transport an Illegal Alien for Profit. Ramos-Mendez was also charged in the complaint with Reentry of Removed Alien. On Oct. 10, 2026, Border Patrol cameras observed a driver in a Dodge Ram traveling south on Federal Route 15 on the Tohono O'odham Nation. The driver, later identified as Calixtro-Rodriguez, performed a u-turn and parked on the side of the road near mile marker 5, a known pick-up spot for illegal aliens. Multiple subjects were observed entering the Dodge Ram. Calixtro-Rodriguez then traveled northbound. Border Patrol Agents (BPAs) attempted to stop him to conduct an immigration inspection, but Calixtro-Rodriguez failed to yield. BPAs then deployed a tire deflation device which disabled the vehicle. All of the subjects bailed from the vehicle and ran away. BPAs were able to apprehend Calixtro-Rodriguez and three passengers, including Ramos-Mendez, who were determined to be citizens of Mexico, unlawfully present in the United States. BPAs learned that Ramos-Mendez was the group's foot guide. Records checks revealed that Ramos-Mendez had been previously removed from the United States and did not have authorization to return. [Case Number: 26-MJ-04143] United States v. Christopher Paul Lopez. On Oct. 9, 2026, Christopher Paul Lopez was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien. On Oct. 8, an Arizona Department of Public Safety Trooper performed a traffic stop on a Land Rover driving on the I-10. The Trooper observed Lopez lying in the rear of the vehicle during the traffic stop. Lopez began reaching for a black bag, prompting the Trooper to ask if the bag contained a firearm, which Lopez confirmed. The Trooper removed the bag and recovered a loaded Glock 19 handgun from inside. The Trooper directed Lopez to exit the vehicle to speak with them. Their conversation led the Trooper to believe Lopez and the driver were involved in human smuggling. BPAs responded to the scene and determined that the driver was a citizen of Mexico, unlawfully present in the United States. BPAs also learned that Lopez had been paid to accompany the driver from Tucson to Phoenix. [Case Number: 26-MJ-8411] United States v. Jose Avendano-Soto. On Oct. 13, 2026, Jose Avendano-Soto was charged by criminal complaint with Transportation of an Illegal Alien. On Oct. 8, 2026, a Border Patrol Agent (BPA) observed an SUV driving directly alongside the US-Mexico border wall before stopping. Seven individuals exited the vehicle and deployed a rope ladder to climb over the wall. Five members of the group continued walking north into the United States. The two remaining individuals covered the group's footprints and returned to Mexico. BPAs found the five individuals later, hiding among vegetation wearing camouflage clothing. BPAs determined four were citizens of Guatemala and that one was a citizen of Mexico, and that all were unlawfully present in the United States. BPAs also learned that one of them, Avendano-Soto, was serving as the group’s foot guide into the United States. [Case Number: 26-MJ-1825] A criminal complaint is a formal accusation of criminal conduct. All defendants are presumed innocent until proven guilty beyond a reasonable doubt in a court of law. title: Be There for the Beginning: Celebrate the Launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark
body: Be There for the Beginning: Celebrate the Launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark Explore a new era of local AI, join launch celebrations around the world and #ShareYourSpark. October 15, 2026 by Shreevar Rastogi 0 Comments Share Share This Article X Facebook LinkedIn Copy link Link copied! A new beginning for Windows PCs starts tomorrow with the launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark — one PC built for creators, gamers and AI agents. All are invited to celebrate with NVIDIA and partners at launch events around the world. Share Your Spark Every PC has a story. What was your first Windows PC, and what did it spark a love for? Join the celebration online by sharing responses with #ShareYourSpark for a chance to win an ASUS ProArt P14 RTX Spark laptop signed by NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang. See the campaign and official rules . See What Reviewers Are Saying From local AI workflows to creative apps and gaming, see what reviewers are saying about RTX Spark — then experience it at a launch celebration. “The fact that NVIDIA, Microsoft and their partners have delivered such a capable, compatible and polished platform even in its first at-bat should put the rest of the PC industry on notice.” — Tom’s Hardware “I tested NVIDIA’s RTX Spark for gaming and local AI – the performance absolutely stunned me.” — TrustedReviews , UK “I’m very happy to report that performance is actually looking really good when it comes to AI, gaming and creative workflows.” — Microcenter “[RTX Spark] is a different species of computer that has arrived early. It is a statement of intent from NVIDIA about where computing is going — trading raw benchmarking crowns for the ability to carry a self-rewriting, fully autonomous, CUDA-accelerated digital brain in your backpack.” — Tom’s Guide “One of the most impressive parts of the launch is how many apps NVIDIA has worked with to ensure optimisation with the Spark technology.” — Creative Bloq Independent testing from Artificial Analysis offers an early look at the powerful local AI performance RTX Spark brings to a laptop. Join the Launch Celebrations On Friday, Oct. 16, get hands on with RTX Spark at launch events around the world. Explore demos for creating, developing and gaming, connect with fellow enthusiasts and discover what local AI can do. Times below are local. Follow each event’s entry instructions. Space is limited. San Francisco — Best Buy, 1717 Harrison Street, 10 a.m.-12 p.m . Try hands-on demos, meet iJustine and hear fireside conversations with local tech founders. Free, first-come, first-served entry; no ticket required. Event details . Berlin — Xperion at Saturn, Alexanderplatz 3, 7-10:30 p.m . Explore hands-on demos and stage programming with creators and developers. Registration required. RSVP . Taipei — Muse Garden, No. 88 Yanchang Road . Join an evening of demos, music and AI community discussions, with shopping and networking continuing until 10:15 p.m. Registration required . Beijing — JD MALL Beijing Shuangjing Store, No. 31 Guangqu Road . Check in begins at 7 p.m. Launch celebration starts at 8 p.m., followed by hands-on demos. Event concludes at 9:30 p.m. Register through WeChat. Istanbul — Vatan Bilgisayar Topkapı, Mevlana Caddesi No. 138 . Explore hands-on demos and local creator programming. Walk-in entry; no advance registration required. Seoul — COEX East Lobby, 513 Yeongdong-daero . Hands-on demos begin at 7 p.m., with gaming and AI creator programming from 8 p.m. Event concludes at 9:30 p.m. No advance registration required. Categories: AI Tags: Local AI NVIDIA RTX RTX AI Garage RTX Spark Related News AI Be There for the Beginning: Celebrate the Launch of NVIDIA RTX Spark Oct 15, 2026 AI Open From Data Center to Desktop: NVIDIA Expands Nemotron Family With Highest Efficiency Super VL and Bolt Models Oct 15, 2026 AI NVIDIA Expands Advanced Technology Access for Europe’s Scientific Community Through Open Learning Resources, Collaborations and Compute Oct 15, 2026 AI NVIDIA Announces New Investments in the UK Startup Ecosystem Oct 13, 2026
